question: What does microbiology study?
explanation: Microbiology specifically focuses on living things and agents that are too small to see without magnification. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why did ancient healers fail to cure infectious diseases effectively?

options.A: They used herbs that neutralized all medicines
options.B: They lacked knowledge of unseen microbes
options.C: They only treated wealthy members of society
options.D: They refused to use clean water supplies

explanation: Without optical instruments, early societies had no way to identify bacteria or viruses as the root cause of infections. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h1)

question: What does the theory of spontaneous generation state?

options.A: Boiling liquids destroys all organic matter
options.B: Diseases are spread through contaminated water
options.D: Microbes only come from other microbes

explanation: Spontaneous generation was the mistaken belief that living organisms could form out of inanimate substances. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h2)

question: What was the main purpose of Louis Pasteur using swan-neck flasks?

options.A: To speed up the evaporation of broth
options.B: To prevent pressure from breaking the glass
options.C: To trap dust while letting air enter
options.D: To heat the liquid to extreme temperatures

explanation: The curved neck allowed air in but trapped airborne particles and microbes, keeping the broth sterile. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h2)

question: Who was the first person to observe bacteria using a simple microscope?
explanation: Leeuwenhoek handcrafted powerful single-lens microscopes and recorded the first descriptions of microorganisms. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h3)

question: How do electron microscopes differ from light microscopes?

options.A: They are small enough to carry in a pocket
options.B: They rely on natural sunlight for illumination
options.C: They produce images in full color automatically
options.D: They use electron beams instead of light

explanation: Using electrons allows for much higher resolution, making it possible to see tiny viruses that light microscopes miss. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of the germ theory of disease?

options.A: Clean air prevents all bacterial growth
options.D: Chemicals can cure any viral infection

explanation: The germ theory replaced older miasma beliefs by proving individual pathogens drive specific diseases. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why must a pathogen be grown in pure culture during Koch's steps?

options.A: To make the bacteria multiply faster
options.B: To destroy any viral particles present
options.C: To change the color of the nutrient agar
options.D: To ensure only one germ is tested

explanation: A pure culture ensures that any symptoms in the test animal come from one specific organism and nothing else. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h4)

question: What disease did Edward Jenner use to protect people against smallpox?
explanation: Jenner used milder cowpox lesions to stimulate immunity against the deadly smallpox virus. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h5)

question: How was penicillin discovered by Alexander Fleming?

options.A: Chemicals in soil cured infected laboratory mice
options.B: A mold contaminant inhibited bacterial growth
options.C: He boiled sewage water until crystals formed
options.D: He tested thousands of plant roots in a lab

explanation: Fleming noticed a fungal spore drifted onto his culture plate and created a clear zone where bacteria could not grow. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is handwashing before and after patient care critical in a Nigerian ward?

options.A: It removes unpleasant odors from the skin
options.C: It prevents skin oils from staining linens
options.D: It breaks the chain of microbial transmission

explanation: Mechanical removal of transient flora through hand hygiene stops pathogens from spreading between patients. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is a major nursing responsibility related to antibiotic therapy?

options.A: Stopping medication as soon as fever drops
options.B: Administering full courses to prevent resistance
options.C: Diluting syrups with water for faster action
options.D: Prescribing stronger drugs for viral colds

explanation: Completing prescribed antibiotic regimens ensures all target pathogens are eliminated, preventing drug-resistant strains. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h6)
